instructions: Unreal Editor tools of the open project. Read tools answer at once; write tools ask the user to confirm in the editor (55 s limit) and run as one undoable transaction that is rolled back as a whole if any object fails. Object paths are full paths such as /Game/Maps/Main.Main:PersistentLevel.Cube_1. Unreal Engine toolsets (UMG, Niagara, PCG and more) are reached through list_toolsets, describe_toolset and call_toolset_tool. When a request is ambiguous, ask_user lets the user pick from your options in the editor.

tools.name: find_assets
tools.description: Find assets in the asset registry by name, class and folder, without loading them. Lists name | class | object path, sorted by name.

query.description: Part of the asset name, case-insensitive; empty matches all.

class.description: Asset class name, e.g. StaticMesh, Material, Blueprint, World; empty matches all.

path.description: Package folder to search, e.g. /Game/Maps. Defaults to /Game.

recursive.description: Search sub-folders too. Defaults to true.

offset.description: Index of the first result, for paging. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: get_asset
tools.description: Details of one asset from the asset registry, without loading it: class, package, registry tags, and how many packages it depends on and are referencing it.

tools.name: get_asset_references
tools.description: Packages an asset depends on, or packages that reference it, from the asset registry. Lists package names, sorted.

path.description: Object path or package name of the asset.

direction.description: dependencies: what the asset uses; referencers: what uses the asset.

offset.description: Index of the first result, for paging. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: list_actors
tools.description: List actors of the level open in the editor (loaded World Partition cells only). Lists label | class | path | location, sorted by label.

class.description: Only actors of this class or a subclass, e.g. StaticMeshActor, PointLight; empty matches all.

query.description: Part of the actor label, case-insensitive; empty matches all.

offset.description: Index of the first result, for paging. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Actors currently selected in the level editor: label | class | path | location.

tools.name: get_properties
tools.description: Property values of one object as editor text (the format set_property accepts): an actor, a component, an asset or a class default object. Each line is Name "Details panel name" [Category] (type) = value. Without names, lists the properties the Details panel shows. A user who names a setting in words means the Details panel name: match it on the object they selected (the actor) before looking at its components.

path.description: Full object path, or the label of an actor in the open level. A component path is the actor path plus .ComponentName.

names.description: Only these properties, by name or Details panel name.

all.description: Include properties the Details panel hides. Defaults to false.

offset.description: Index of the first property, for paging. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: describe_class
tools.description: A class's parent chain, editable properties with their types, and Blueprint-callable functions; optionally the class default values.

class.description: Class name (StaticMeshActor), script path (/Script/Engine.StaticMeshActor) or Blueprint asset path.

defaults.description: Show each property's class default value. Defaults to false.

offset.description: Index of the first line, for paging. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Project settings and editor preferences pages (UDeveloperSettings). Without a class, lists the pages as class | container / category / section; with one, its current values.

class.description: Settings class name, e.g. RendererSettings; empty lists the pages.

offset.description: Index of the first line, for paging. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: read_log
tools.description: The latest lines of the editor's Output Log since the editor started, oldest first: time [category] verbosity: text.

level.description: Least severe level to include. Defaults to log.

category.description: Only this log category, e.g. LogTemp, LogBlueprint; empty includes all.

tools.name: get_cvar
tools.description: A console variable's value, flags and help; or, with query, the console variables and commands whose names contain it.

name.description: Exact console variable name, e.g. r.ScreenPercentage.

query.description: Part of a name to search for, used when name is empty.

offset.description: Index of the first search result, for paging. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Search results per page, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user to choose before you act, when a request is ambiguous and the choice decides what changes (which object, which value, which of several matches). The user sees the question with your options as buttons in the editor panel and must answer within about a minute; the result is their answer. Do not use it for questions you can settle with read tools.

question.description: The question, short and in the user's language.

options.description: 2-6 short answers to choose from, in the user's language, most likely first.

allow_other.description: Whether the user may write an answer of their own. Defaults to true.

tools.name: get_material_parameters
tools.description: Every parameter of materials or material instances in one call: name, group, type (scalar, vector, texture, static switch), current value and, for instances, whether it is overridden or inherited; plus the parent chain. Pass actors instead to list the materials on each slot of their mesh components. Prefer this over reading parameters one by one.

targets.description: Material or material instance asset paths, actor labels or paths in the open level, or mesh component paths.

tools.name: set_property
tools.description: Set one property to the same value on one or more objects (actors, components, assets), as the Details panel would. The value uses editor text format, the same get_properties prints: 1.5, true, (X=0,Y=0,Z=100), /Game/Mat/M_Red.M_Red. When the user names a setting in words, it is the Details panel name of the object they selected (usually the actor itself, not its components); check it with get_properties first. The user confirms first; it runs as one undoable step and is rolled back as a whole if any object fails.

targets.description: Full object paths, or labels of actors in the open level.

property.description: Property name or Details panel name, as get_properties lists it.

value.description: New value in editor text format.

tools.name: spawn_actor
tools.description: Place a new actor in the open level, from a native class or a Blueprint. The user confirms first; it runs as one undoable step.

class.description: Actor class name (PointLight), script path, or Blueprint asset path (/Game/BP/BP_Door).

location.description: Location [x, y, z] in cm. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].

rotation.description: Rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].

label.description: Actor label shown in the Outliner; defaults to the class name.

tools.name: delete_actors
tools.description: Delete actors from the open level. The user confirms first; it runs as one undoable step and is rolled back as a whole if any actor fails.

targets.description: Full actor paths, or labels of actors in the open level.

tools.name: save_assets
tools.description: Save assets or levels to disk. Saving cannot be undone from the editor; the user confirms first. Source control may ask the user to check files out.

targets.description: Object paths or package names of the assets or levels to save.

all_dirty.description: Save every asset and level with unsaved changes instead. Defaults to false.

tools.name: set_material_parameters
tools.description: Change several parameters on one or more material instances in one step, e.g. the same color on eight instances; the user confirms one card listing every instance and parameter with its current and planned value. Values: scalar as a number; vector as [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] (linear 0-1) or "#RRGGBB" (sRGB); texture as an asset path, or "None"; static switch as true / false (recompiles the material). Base materials cannot be changed this way: create instances with create_material_instances. Runs as one undoable step, rolled back as a whole if any instance fails. Prefer this over changing parameters one at a time.

parameters.description: Parameter name to new value, e.g. {"BaseColor": [1, 0, 0], "Roughness": 0.4}. Every instance must have every parameter.

tools.name: create_material_instances
tools.description: Create several material instance assets of one parent material in one step, optionally with parameter values (same value format as set_material_parameters). Fails if an asset of that name already exists. New assets cannot be undone from the editor; they stay unsaved until save_assets. Prefer this over creating instances one at a time.

parent.description: Parent material or material instance asset path.

names.description: Asset names of the new instances, e.g. MI_Wall_Red.

folder.description: Package folder for the new assets, e.g. /Game/Materials/Walls. Defaults to the parent's folder.

parameters.description: Parameter name to value, set on every new instance.

tools.name: assign_material
tools.description: Put a material or material instance on placed actors in the open level, as a per-component override like the Details panel's Materials list. Only those actors change: the mesh asset and every other placement of it keep their materials. Without slots, every slot of every mesh component of the targets is set. Runs as one undoable step, rolled back as a whole if any slot fails.

targets.description: Actor labels or paths in the open level, or mesh component paths.

material.description: Material or material instance asset path.

slots.description: Slots to set, by index ("0") or slot name, as get_material_parameters lists them. Defaults to every slot.

tools.name: tidy_graph
tools.description: Tidy the node layout of a node-graph asset: Blueprints (event graphs, functions, macros, Animation and Widget Blueprints), materials and material functions, Control Rigs, and other assets that keep a node graph. Nodes flow left to right in columns, rows follow pin order to reduce crossing wires, separate node groups are stacked, unconnected nodes go to one side, and comment boxes are resized to keep wrapping their nodes. Pass nodes to arrange only those (for example the nodes you just added) and leave the rest where the user put them; nodes takes the titles the editor shows (Branch, Print String) or object names, and a title shared by several nodes arranges all of them; arrange whole graphs only when the user asks for it. Sizes come from the asset's open editor, otherwise they are estimated. A material open in the Material Editor has its working graph arranged; the user applies or saves it there. Runs as one undoable step.

graph.description: Only this graph, e.g. EventGraph or a function name. Defaults to every graph of the asset; an error lists the graph names.

nodes.description: Only these nodes, by object name or by the title the editor shows; the other nodes stay where they are and anchor the arranged ones. Defaults to every node.

tools.name: place_actors
tools.description: Place many new actors in the open level in one step: copies of a static mesh, Blueprint or actor class, or duplicates of an actor already in the level (keeping its settings). Layouts: grid (rows x columns), line (origin to end, or along a direction), circle (around a center), spline (along a spline actor, optionally to one side), scatter (random within an area, keeping min_distance). Optional random yaw and scale, dropping onto the ground, an Outliner folder and a label. Up to 500 per call; the user confirms one card listing every new actor's transform; it runs as one undoable step. Use this instead of calling spawn_actor many times.

source.description: What to place: asset path (/Game/Props/SM_Rock, a Blueprint), actor class name (PointLight), or the label of an actor in the open level to duplicate.

label.description: Label for the new actors, numbered _1, _2 ... Defaults to the source name.

folder.description: Outliner folder for the new actors, e.g. Props/Rocks.

pattern.description: How to lay the new actors out.

origin.description: [x, y, z] cm: grid corner, line start, circle center or scatter center.

end.description: line: [x, y, z] cm end point; without spacing the first and last actor sit on origin and end.

direction.description: line without end: [x, y, z] direction from origin. Defaults to [1, 0, 0].

spacing.description: cm between neighbours: grid along X (and Y unless spacing_y), line, spline.

spacing_y.description: grid: cm between rows along Y. Defaults to spacing.

spline.description: spline: label or path of an actor with a spline component (or the component path).

side_offset.description: spline: cm to the right of the spline, negative to the left; call twice for both sides of a road.

area.description: scatter: label or path of an actor (e.g. a volume) whose bounds are the area.

extent.description: scatter without area: [x, y] half sizes in cm around origin.

min_distance.description: scatter: least cm between any two actors. Defaults to 0.

rotation.description: [pitch, yaw, roll] degrees for every actor. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].

face_center.description: circle: turn each actor's front (+X) to the center.

follow_path.description: line, circle, spline: turn each actor's front (+X) along the path.

random_yaw.description: Random extra yaw within ± this many degrees.

random_scale.description: [min, max] random uniform scale factor, e.g. [0.8, 1.2].

snap_to_ground.description: Drop each actor straight down until its bottom rests on what is below. Defaults to false.

seed.description: Random seed for scatter and random_*; the same arguments give the same result.

count.description: How many: line, circle, spline, scatter. Line and spline may use spacing instead.

tools.name: arrange_actors
tools.description: Move existing actors of the open level in one step. operation: align (same coordinate on one axis: min, max, center or a value), distribute (spread evenly along one axis between the two outermost, keeping their order), snap_to_ground (drop each until its bottom rests on what is below), pattern (move them into a grid, line, circle, spline or scatter layout, in the order given; origin defaults to the first target), randomize (random yaw and scale). The user confirms one card listing each actor's current and planned transform; it runs as one undoable step. Use this instead of setting each actor's location with set_property.

targets.description: Actor labels or paths in the open level; for pattern, their order is the layout order.

operation.description: What to do with the targets.

align_to.description: align: line up on the smallest, largest or middle coordinate, or on value. Defaults to center.

value.description: align_to value: the coordinate in cm.

pattern.description: For operation pattern: the layout to move the targets into, in the order given.

origin.description: [x, y, z] cm: grid corner, line start, circle center or scatter center. Defaults to the first target's location.

end.description: line: [x, y, z] cm end point; without spacing the first and last actor sit on origin and end.

direction.description: line without end: [x, y, z] direction from origin. Defaults to [1, 0, 0].

spacing.description: cm between neighbours: grid along X (and Y unless spacing_y), line, spline.

spacing_y.description: grid: cm between rows along Y. Defaults to spacing.

rows.description: Unused by arrange_actors; columns decides the rows.

columns.description: grid: columns along X. Defaults to a square-ish grid.

spline.description: spline: label or path of an actor with a spline component (or the component path).

side_offset.description: spline: cm to the right of the spline, negative to the left; call twice for both sides of a road.

area.description: scatter: label or path of an actor (e.g. a volume) whose bounds are the area.

extent.description: scatter without area: [x, y] half sizes in cm around origin.

min_distance.description: scatter: least cm between any two actors. Defaults to 0.

rotation.description: [pitch, yaw, roll] degrees for every target; without it targets keep their own rotation unless face_center or follow_path.

face_center.description: circle: turn each actor's front (+X) to the center.

follow_path.description: line, circle, spline: turn each actor's front (+X) along the path.

random_yaw.description: Random extra yaw within ± this many degrees.

random_scale.description: [min, max] random uniform scale factor, e.g. [0.8, 1.2].

snap_to_ground.description: Drop each actor straight down until its bottom rests on what is below. Defaults to false.

seed.description: Random seed for scatter and random_*; the same arguments give the same result.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the editor's most recent steps, as Ctrl+Z would; this includes steps the user made by hand. The user confirms first and sees which steps.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the editor's most recently undone steps, as Ctrl+Y would. The user confirms first and sees which steps.

tools.name: list_toolsets
tools.description: List the Unreal Engine toolsets enabled in this editor (UMG, Niagara, PCG, Gameplay Tags, StateTree and more), with what each is for. They hold many more editor tools than this server's own. Use describe_toolset to see a toolset's tools, then call_toolset_tool. Prefer this server's own tools when one fits.

tools.name: describe_toolset
tools.description: Show an engine toolset's tools, each marked read (runs at once) or write (the user confirms first). Pass tool to see that tool's full description and its arguments schema before calling it.

toolset.description: Toolset name exactly as list_toolsets gives it.

tool.description: One tool's name, to see its description and arguments; leave out to list the toolset's tools.

tools.name: call_toolset_tool
tools.description: Run one engine toolset tool. Read tools answer at once; every other tool asks the user to confirm first (55 s limit) and runs as one step, undoable where the engine records it. Check the tool's arguments with describe_toolset first.

toolset.description: Toolset name exactly as list_toolsets gives it.

tool.description: Tool name as describe_toolset gives it.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments as its schema in describe_toolset describes them; leave out when it takes none.
